Generate an initrd with the supplied root filesystem's mkinitramfs.

## Inputs

| Name             | Kind      | Description                                                               |
| ---------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rootfs`         | directory | Root filesystem containing mkinitramfs, hooks, and target kernel modules. |
| `kernel-version` | file      | Text file containing one kernel version.                                  |

## Outputs

| Name     | Kind | Description                                                     |
| -------- | ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `initrd` | file | Initrd generated by the supplied root filesystem's mkinitramfs. |

## Execution

| Setting      | Value        |
| ------------ | ------------ |
| Environment  | Rugix Bakery |
| Source epoch | Consumed     |
| Output cache | Allowed      |

## Behavior

Generate an initrd with a prepared Debian root filesystem's `mkinitramfs`. The
`kernel-version` input is a text file containing one installed kernel version,
optionally followed by a newline. Use `core/kernel-debian` to select a kernel
and produce this file.

The root filesystem must contain `mkinitramfs`, target kernel modules, and the
required initramfs hooks. Its programs must run on the builder, either natively
or through configured emulation. The rule uses a disposable copy and leaves the
input root filesystem unchanged.

The build source epoch is passed as `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`. Custom hooks must also
avoid clocks, randomness, and undeclared external state for reproducible
initrds.

## Example

For example, generate an initrd for a selected kernel:

```toml
uses = "core/initrd-debian"
inputs.rootfs = { path = "prepared-root" }
inputs.kernel-version = { path = "kernel-version" }
```

Save the invocation as `build-rule.toml` and run
`./run-bakery bake rule build-rule.toml build/result`. The output is `initrd`.
